title: Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira
body:
For: Jira admins and project admins. You will learn: what the app does, who it is for and where to start.

Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira inside a Jira project.

See every Jira workflow. Change it safely.

Jira workflows grow until nobody knows exactly what they do: conditions that point to deleted groups, users who left, Done transitions that never set a resolution, rules of apps you no longer use. Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira reads your workflows live from Jira, explains them in plain language, finds what is broken and helps you fix it. Looking never changes anything. A change only happens when you confirm it, Jira checks it first, and you can undo it with one click.

How it works

From setup to everyday use in four steps.

What you can do

 #FFF4EE :mag:

Understand every workflow

Overview with health score and action plan.

Diagram, transition table and every rule, including rules of other apps, in plain words. A health score and a prioritised action plan per project, or for the whole site. Export it all as HTML, PDF, CSV or JSON.

 #EAF2FF :link:

Know the impact first

Every transition that uses a group, at a glance.

See every transition that depends on a group, role, field, user, screen or app before you delete or rename it. The access simulator shows who can move an issue, and why someone can't.

 #E9F7EF :white_check_mark:

Fix problems safely

An Autopilot plan, validated by Jira.

The Autopilot turns findings into a change plan. You see the health score before and after, Jira validates the plan, a backup is stored, and one click rolls it back.

Who it is for

 #F4F5F7 :busts_in_silhouette:

Project admins

Open the app in Project settings › Apps. Analyse every workflow of your project, check the impact of a change, fix findings and change the team-managed workflows of your own project.

Read the user guide

 #F4F5F7 :shield:

Jira admins

Everything project admins can do, plus a site-wide page: analyse every workflow on the site, change company-managed and shared workflows, change many workflows at once and decide whether the AI features are switched on.

Read the admin guide

Explore the documentation

title: Workflow Analyzer – Getting started
body:
For: the Jira admin who installs the app, and project admins opening it for the first time. You will learn: how to install the app, what Jira asks you to approve, where to find the app and what to do first.

 2

Before you start

  • You need Jira Cloud. The app works with company-managed and team-managed projects.
  • To install the app you must be a Jira admin (someone who can manage apps on your site).
  • To use the app in a project you must be a project admin of that project (or a Jira admin). Other users don't see any data.

Step 1: Install the app

Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira is available on the Atlassian Marketplace.

  1. In Jira, open Apps › Explore more apps.
  2. Search for Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira and open it.
  3. Start the free trial or subscribe, and follow the steps Jira shows you.
  4. Approve the permissions (see the next section). Jira installs the app in a few seconds.

Sites with up to 10 users can use the app for free. Atlassian bills larger sites per user.

What Jira asks you to approve, and why

During the install, Jira lists what the app may do. In plain words:

PermissionWhy the app needs it
Read Jira project and issue dataRead workflows, statuses, transitions, rules, screens, fields, resolutions, roles and issue counts to build the analysis.
Write Jira project and issue dataOnly when you click a button for it: create Jira tasks from findings (Create Jira tasks) and repair the resolution of issues (Review & repair).
Read user informationCheck your permissions and show the names of users and groups that workflow rules refer to, for example inactive users.
Manage Jira configurationWorkflows are part of the site configuration. The Autopilot needs this to apply and roll back the changes you confirm. Company-managed workflows can only be changed by Jira admins.
Store data in the app's own storageKeep change plans and backups, snapshots, team notes, monitoring status, your preferences, the AI switch and the AI usage meter, inside Atlassian.
Report personal dataTell Atlassian which account IDs the app stores, so it can delete them when an account is closed (GDPR).

The app also includes AI features (Atlassian's Forge LLMs and the Rovo agent Workflow Analyst). They stay off until a Jira admin switches them on. More in Security & privacy.

Step 2: Find the app in Jira

WhereWhoWhat you get
Project settings › Apps › Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for JiraProject admins and Jira adminsThe analysis of all workflows used by this project.
Jira settings › Apps › Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira (site-wide)Jira admins onlyThe analysis of every workflow on the site, bulk changes and the AI switch.
Rovo chat › Agents › Workflow AnalystProject admins and Jira admins, for the projects they administer. Only when Rovo is enabled on your site and a Jira admin has switched the AI features on.Ask questions about workflows and plan changes in chat.

The app in Project settings: tabs at the top, the workflow selector on the right.

Step 3: Your first steps

  1. Open the app in a project you administer. The app reads the workflows live from Jira. There is nothing to upload and no field mapping.
  2. Take the tour. On the Overview, the New here? tip offers Start the tour (1 minute) and Open the guide. You can start the tour again at any time with the ? button in the header.
  3. Choose your language with DE / EN in the top right. The app remembers your choice.
  4. Pick a workflow in the Workflow selector if the project uses several, or keep All workflows.
  5. Look at the Overview: the Health score (0–100), the Action plan sorted by priority, and the Health check per area. Click an action to see the findings behind it.
#EAF2FF :shield:

Jira admins: two more steps

  1. Open Jira settings › Apps › Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira (site-wide) and click Scan all workflows. The scan only reads and takes a few seconds per 100 workflows.
  2. Decide about the AI features card on the same page. AI is off by default. Click Turn on only if your organisation wants it. Every feature without AI works either way.

The site-wide page before the first scan, with the AI features card (switched on in this example).

You're done when…

#E9F7EF :white_check_mark:
  • The app opens in Project settings › Apps and shows a health score for your project.
  • You know where the ? button (tour) and the Guide tab are.
  • Jira admins: the site-wide page shows the scan result, and you have decided whether the AI features stay off or are switched on.

Next: the User guide shows every task step by step.

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Workflow Analyzer – User guide
body:
For: project admins (and Jira admins) who work with the app in a project. You will learn: how to understand your workflows, check the impact of a change, fix findings, change workflows safely with the Autopilot and export documentation.

 2

Golden rules for safe use

#FFF4EE :shield:
  1. Looking is always safe. Overview, Diagram, Transitions, Access, Flow, Dependencies, Explanations, Health check, Compare and Export only read data.
  2. Jira changes only when you confirm it: when you apply or roll back an Autopilot plan (Apply to Jira, Roll back), repair issue resolutions (Yes, repair) or create Jira tasks from findings. Never automatically, never by the AI alone.
  3. Read every plan before you apply it: the operations, the preview, the health score before and after, and any new findings.
  4. Try bigger changes in a test project first, for example a copy of your project.
  5. Watch the "shared workflow" warning. A change to a shared workflow affects every project listed.
  6. Know where Roll back is: Autopilot › select the plan › Roll back.
  7. Use project roles and groups in rules, not individual users.
  8. Exports contain names of users, groups and fields. Share them only internally.

Find your way around

Open the app in Project settings › Apps › Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira. The tabs are grouped in three steps:

UnderstandCheck and changeDocument
Overview · Diagram · Transitions · Access · Flow · Dependencies · Explanations (called AI assistant when AI is on) Health check · Compare · Autopilot · Changes Export · Guide
  • Workflow selector (right of the tabs): projects can use a different workflow per issue type. Pick one to focus every tab on it, or keep All workflows.
  • Search (header): jump to any status, transition, group, field or app.
  • Refresh reads the workflows from Jira again. ? starts the 1-minute tour. DE / EN switches the language.
  • The badge next to the project key shows your role: Jira admin (all workflows) or Project admin (this project).
  • The Guide tab has a step-by-step guide inside the app.

Keyboard shortcuts: / search, Alt+1…9 switch tabs, Esc closes panels.

Get an overview of your workflows

  1. Open the Overview tab.
  2. Read the Health score (0–100): GreenHealthy YellowNeeds attention RedAt risk. It starts at 100 and goes down for every problem, most for serious ones.
  3. Check the tiles: Workflows, Rules, Dependencies (with how many are "not found") and Apps in use.
  4. Work through the Action plan. It groups the findings into actions with a priority (P1 fix soon, P2 plan it, P3 nice to have) and an effort. Click an action to see its findings in the health check.
  5. The Health check card on the right scores five areas: Structure, Data quality, Access control, Integrity and Maintainability.

The Overview: health score, tiles, action plan and health check per area.

If issues have a resolution that does not match their status, a banner at the top offers Review & repair (see Repair issue resolutions below).

Read a workflow diagram

  1. Pick a workflow in the Workflow selector, then open Diagram.
  2. Click a status to highlight its transitions. Click a transition label for its details.
  3. Drag to pan, use the zoom buttons and Fit. Switch between Jira layout and Auto layout.
  4. Use Overlay to colour the diagram by Issue load (after loading live data in the Flow tab), Persona access or Impact of a group or app.
  5. Download the diagram as SVG, PNG or Mermaid (Mermaid is also copied to the clipboard, ready for Confluence, GitHub or Markdown).

The workflow diagram straight from Jira, with app rules and findings highlighted.

Look up the rules of a transition

  1. Open Transitions. Every status lists its transitions with Screen, Properties, Conditions, Validators and Post functions in plain language.
  2. Narrow the table with App filter (for example JMWE, JSU, ScriptRunner, or Only third-party) and Element filter. Choose the visible Columns.
  3. Click a transition name to see What this transition does: who can run it, what is checked and what happens afterwards.
  4. Add a Note for your team. All admins of the project see it in the app.
  5. Select rows and click Export selection to get an HTML file with just those transitions.

Find out what depends on a group, field or app

Do this before you delete a group, uninstall an app, rename a field or deactivate a user.

  1. Open Dependencies.
  2. Choose a type: Apps, Groups, Project roles, Fields, Users, Screens, Statuses or Permissions.
  3. Select an entry. The right side lists every Affected transition with workflow, path and rule.
  4. Click Show in diagram to see the impact in the workflow graph, or Export matrix (CSV) for Excel.

The Dependency & impact finder: the group "legal" is used in three transitions.

Entries marked Rednot found no longer exist on the site (deleted or renamed). Rules that depend on them may block transitions.

Check a whole list at once: click Check a list, paste several groups, roles, fields, users or apps (one per line or separated by commas) and click Check. Each name shows in use, not used or not found.

This check covers workflows only. Groups can also be used in permission schemes, notification schemes, filters, dashboards or boards. Check those before you delete a group.

Find out who can move an issue

Use this for "why can't I move this ticket?" requests.

  1. Open Access and stay in Persona simulator.
  2. Under Persona, tick everything the person is or belongs to: reporter, assignee, groups, project roles. With nothing ticked you see what every user can do.
  3. Read the result per status: Greenallowed Redblocked Yellowdepends, each with the reason.
  4. Switch to Path finder to see how an issue gets from status A to B, optionally only with transitions the persona may use.
  5. Switch to Who-can-do-what matrix for all groups and roles at once.

The access simulator: "Approve" is blocked because the persona is not in the allowed group or role.

"depends" means the result depends on data of the actual issue (field values, history) or on an app condition that is only checked when the transition runs.

Find bottlenecks with the live flow

  1. Open Flow and click Load live data. The app counts the issues per status (respecting your Jira permissions).
  2. Set Stale after to the number of days after which an untouched issue counts as stale.
  3. Read the Insights: Bottleneck, Stale and Unused statuses. Check unused statuses before you remove one.

Get a workflow explained

  1. Open Explanations. Workflow explained describes the selected workflow in a few sentences: statuses, issue types, where work starts and ends, apps and health findings.
  2. Use Explain a transition to pick any transition and read what it does.

When a Jira admin has switched the AI features on, the tab is called AI assistant and also offers Ask your workflows (see Ask questions and describe changes in your own words (AI) below).

Run the health check and fix findings

  1. Open Health check. Filter by severity: RedCritical YellowWarning BlueHint GreyInfo.
  2. Read each finding and its Recommendation. Show transition jumps to the cause.
  3. Findings marked auto-fix can be repaired by the app: click Fix automatically on one finding, or Fix N automatically at the top for all of them. The app creates an Autopilot plan for you to review. Nothing changes yet.
  4. To plan the work instead, click Task on a finding or Create Jira tasks for all. Choose the Issue type and click Create N task(s). Tasks get the labels workflow-health and superport-wfa, and duplicates are skipped.

The health check with "Fix 8 automatically", the Issue resolutions card and the first findings.

The health check finds, among others: dead ends, unreachable statuses, Done transitions that miss or clear the resolution, Done transitions that fire the Generic Event (so no "resolved" emails), global transitions without conditions, references to deleted groups, inactive or hard-coded users, disabled rules, app rules that depend on an active app licence, very complex transitions and workflows no project uses.

Repair issue resolutions

A workflow fix only helps issues that move from now on. Issues that are already Done, but Unresolved count as open in every filter, report and dashboard, and Open, but resolved issues count as finished. You can repair them without changing their status.

  1. In Health check, find the Issue resolutions card and click Review & repair.
  2. Check the list. The app suggests a resolution per status (Suggestion per status). Change single issues or use Set selected to.
  3. Click Set resolution on N issues or Clear resolution on N issues and confirm with Yes, repair.
  4. Check the summary. Every run appears in the Repair history.
  • Setting a resolution cannot be undone here: Jira cannot take a resolution back without moving the issue. Check your choices first.
  • Clearing a resolution runs the workflow's own transition into the issue's current status. The status stays, Jira records the transition and may send notifications. You can undo a clearing run with Undo.
  • As a project admin, repairs work only when the Resolution field is on the issue's edit screen, and Jira may send notification mails. A Jira admin can repair any issue without mails.
  • Issues changed by someone else in the meantime are never overwritten.

Change a workflow with the Autopilot

The Autopilot turns a fix or a template into a plan. Nothing changes in Jira until you apply the plan.

  1. Create a plan. Open Autopilot and click Auto-fix findings, or open Templates (Cancel transition, Required fields, Restrict transition), fill in the form and click Create plan.
  2. Review the plan. Check every operation (✓ possible, ✕ not possible and skipped), the Preview of changes, the Health score before → after, findings fixed and new findings. Jira validates the plan right away: "Jira has validated this plan – it can be applied."
  3. Check who is affected. If the workflow is shared with other projects, the plan lists them. Tick I understand – apply for all these projects only if the change is right for all of them.
  4. Apply. Click Apply to Jira and confirm with Yes, apply. The app checks the plan against the latest version of the workflow, lets Jira validate it, stores a snapshot and a backup, then updates the workflow.
  5. Verify. Open Diagram and Health check, and try the changed transition with a test issue.

An auto-fix plan: health score 65 → 85, validated by Jira, ready to apply.

Each plan shows where it stands: GreyPlanned → BlueValidated by Jira → GreenApplied → PurpleRollback ready.

  • Use on another workflow creates the same changes for a different workflow. Check the result before applying.
  • Discard removes a plan you don't need.
  • Plans older than 7 days are expired. If the workflow changed since the plan was made, the plan says so. Click Plan again on the current version.
  • Company-managed workflows can only be changed by a Jira admin. As a project admin you can still plan and validate the change and hand it over. You can change the team-managed workflows of your own project.
  • Removing a status moves its issues to the status you choose. A rollback restores the status, but not the previous status of those issues.
  • The Autopilot cannot edit rules of other apps (JMWE, ScriptRunner …). Change them in that app.

Roll back a change

  1. Open Autopilot and select the applied plan in Change plans.
  2. Click Roll back and confirm with Yes, roll back. The workflow is restored exactly as it was before the plan.

If someone changed the workflow after your plan was applied, the app warns you first: a rollback would also undo those later changes. Choose Roll back anyway only if that is what you want.

Ask questions and describe changes in your own words (AI)

These features appear only when a Jira admin has switched the AI features on. The AI runs on Atlassian; your data stays in Atlassian's cloud.

  • Ask your workflows (tab AI assistant): ask a question in plain language. The answer uses the live analysis of this project and is marked AI-generated – please review.
  • Plan with AI (tab Autopilot): describe the change with exact names, for example "Add a status Escalated reachable from Review, only for the role Administrators, with a way back". The Autopilot turns it into a plan you review like any other plan. Plan in Rovo chat does the same in Rovo.
  • Fix with AI (tab Health check): for findings without an automatic fix, the app writes a precise change request for the Autopilot.
  • Ask Rovo and the Rovo agent Workflow Analyst: ask for overviews, usages, health checks and access checks in Rovo chat, or let it plan, apply and roll back changes. It always shows the plan and asks for your confirmation first.

"Plan with AI": a request in plain English becomes a plan you review before anything changes.

The AI assistant answers with this project's live analysis; "Workflow explained" on the right needs no AI.

AI can misunderstand a request. Always read the list of operations before you apply a plan. Name the workflow, the exact status and transition names and the groups or roles. One change per request gives the clearest plans.

Compare two workflows

  1. Open Compare (shown when the project uses at least two workflows).
  2. Choose two workflows. Use Swap to change sides.
  3. Read the summary: identical, different, only in A, only in B. Similar workflows lists pairs with 60% similarity or more. Pairs with 90% or more are candidates for merging into one workflow.

Track changes with snapshots and daily monitoring

  1. Open Changes. Enter a label, for example "Before release 2.4", and click Save snapshot before larger changes.
  2. Later, click Compare with current on a snapshot to see exactly which workflows, statuses, transitions and rules were added, removed or changed.
  3. Click Enable monitoring once per project. The app checks the project every day, saves a snapshot whenever the workflows change and shows a banner on your next visit.

Change tracking: save a snapshot and switch on daily monitoring.

When you come back, Since your last visit shows new and resolved findings, with Show new findings to jump straight to them.

Export documentation

  1. Open Export.
  2. Optional: enter a Customer code and a Workflow label (they control the file name). Choose the Export language and the Content (all workflows or the selected one).
  3. Under Include, tick what you need: Diagram, Transition table, Dependencies, Health check, Plain-language guide, Team notes.
  4. Click Download HTML, Download PDF, Download CSV or Download JSON.

Export documentation as HTML, PDF, CSV or JSON.

FormatBest for
HTMLAn interactive guide in one file with search and filters. Open it locally, print it or paste it into a Confluence HTML macro.
PDFA print-ready report for audits and sign-offs.
CSVThe transition matrix for Excel (semicolon separated), including what happens, who, why and how to fix problems.
JSONThe full analysis for further processing.

Every export explains each workflow in plain words: a verdict, the usual path from start to done (who may take each step, what Jira checks, what happens automatically and why), other routes, prioritised improvements with the reason and the fix, every transition explained and a glossary. The full rule table follows for administrators.

Exports contain names of users, groups and fields. Store them in internal spaces only.

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Workflow Analyzer – Admin guide
body:
For: Jira admins (global permission "Administer Jira"). You will learn: who can do what in the app, how to use the site-wide page and bulk changes, how to switch the AI features on or off, and how licence, app status and uninstalling work.

 2

Understand roles and permissions

The app works out each user's role from their Jira permissions, checked on the server on every call. There is nothing to configure.

RoleCan seeCan change
Jira admin
("Administer Jira")		Every project's page and the site-wide pageAll workflows, including company-managed workflows shared by several projects, and bulk changes. Turns the AI features on or off.
Project admin
("Administer projects" in that project)		The app page of their own projectTeam-managed workflows of their own project. Company-managed workflows: plan and validate only, then hand over to a Jira admin.
Anyone elseNothing ("No access to this page")Nothing

Every change runs with the permissions of the person who confirms it. Creating Jira tasks from findings also needs the "Create issues" permission in the project.

Analyse every workflow on the site

  1. Open Jira settings › Apps › Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira (site-wide).
  2. Click Scan all workflows. The scan only reads: every workflow, its rules and which projects use it. It takes a few seconds per 100 workflows.
  3. Work with the tabs as in a project. On the site-wide page the Workflow selector shows which projects use each workflow.

The site-wide analysis: one health score and action plan for every workflow on the site.

The site-wide page has the same tabs as a project, with these differences:

  • Bulk Autopilot replaces Autopilot: change many workflows at once.
  • Settings holds the AI features switch.
  • Flow (live issue counts) and Changes (snapshots, daily monitoring) are only on project pages.
  • Dependencies › Check a list checks every workflow on the site, so you can see whether a group is still used anywhere before you delete it.
  • Health check › Issue resolutions covers issues in all projects you can see.

Change company-managed and shared workflows

Only Jira admins can apply plans to company-managed workflows. Project admins can plan and validate such a change and hand it over to you.

  1. Open the app in the project, go to Autopilot and select the plan.
  2. Review the operations, the preview and the health score before → after.
  3. If the workflow is shared, the plan names every project that uses it (projects you cannot see are counted, not named). Tick I understand – apply for all these projects only if the change is right for all of them. Otherwise, give the project its own workflow first.
  4. Click Apply to Jira and confirm. A backup and a snapshot are stored, and Roll back is ready.

Every apply is checked again against the latest version of the workflow, so a colleague's edits are never overwritten. A double click or two admins at once change Jira only once.

Change many workflows at once

  1. On the site-wide page, open Bulk Autopilot.
  2. Under Target workflows, filter by what the workflows use, tick only active if needed and click Select shown, or pick workflows one by one (up to 200 per bulk change).
  3. Under Change, choose a template: Remove group/role/user, Replace group/role/user, Resolution on Done, Restrict transitions, Required fields or Operations JSON. With AI on, Describe (AI) lets you write the change in your own words.
  4. Click Dry run for N workflows. Every workflow gets its own plan, Jira validation and health impact. Nothing is changed in Jira yet.
  5. Review the results, confirm shared workflows, and click Apply to N workflows. You see live progress, and you can Stop after the current workflow.
  6. To undo, click Roll back N applied. Each workflow is restored on its own.

Recent bulk changes lists earlier runs. Team-managed workflows are skipped automatically by Resolution on Done, because Jira sets the resolution there.

Site-wide auto-fix: in the site-wide Health check, Fix N automatically opens Bulk Autopilot with one plan per workflow, each with its own repairs.

Turn the AI features on or off

The AI features are Greyoff by default. Only Jira admins can change this.

  1. Open the site-wide page. The AI features card is on the start page, and after the scan in the Settings tab.
  2. Click Turn on (or Turn off).
  3. Tell your project admins. The AI features appear for them after they reload the page, or when they return to the open app.

The AI features card with this month's AI budget and usage.

What the switch controlsWhat works without AI
  • AI chat Ask your workflows
  • Plan with AI, Plan in Rovo chat, Fix with AI, Ask Rovo
  • Bulk Describe (AI)
  • The Rovo agent Workflow Analyst (all its actions are paused while AI is off)
  • All analysis tabs and plain-language explanations
  • Health check, Auto-fix findings and templates
  • Reviewing, applying and rolling back plans
  • Exports

While AI is off, the app hides every AI entry point. The AI assistant tab is called Explanations.

#EAF2FF :bar_chart:

AI budget and usage

  • The AI runs on Atlassian (Forge LLMs and Rovo). Nothing is sent outside Atlassian.
  • A monthly AI budget per site is included in your subscription, at no extra cost. By default it is €20, at most 1,000 AI requests and 2,000,000 tokens per calendar month (UTC). The limits are set by SUPERPORT.
  • The card shows this month's budget, requests and tokens, and who last changed the switch and when.
  • When the budget is used up, the app says "The monthly AI quota is used up. It is available again from the 1st of next month." Everything without AI keeps working.
  • If SUPERPORT has to turn the AI off for a while, the card says "Temporarily turned off by the app vendor. Your setting is kept."

The Rovo agent also needs Rovo to be enabled on your site.

Repair issue resolutions without notification mails

Jira admins can repair the resolution of any issue silently: only the Resolution field changes, the status stays, no notification mails are sent and the change appears in the issue history. Project admins can repair only issues whose edit screen has the Resolution field, and Jira may send mails. See User guide › Repair issue resolutions for the steps.

See who changed what

The app has no separate audit log page. Instead, every change is recorded where it happened:

WhatWhere you see it
Change plans: who created, applied or rolled back a plan, and whenAutopilot › Change plans (project) and Bulk Autopilot › Recent bulk changes (site)
Issue resolution repairsHealth check › Issue resolutions › Repair history
Snapshots and daily monitoringChanges tab of each project
The AI switchAI features card: "Last changed … by …"
Workflow changes themselvesJira, as with any workflow change made by that user

Manage the licence

Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira is a paid app, billed by Atlassian. Sites with up to 10 users can use it for free.

  • Start a free trial or subscribe under Apps › Manage your apps.
  • Without an active licence, the app shows "Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira needs an active licence" and the daily monitoring pauses. Saved plans, snapshots and notes are kept.

Check the app status

If SUPERPORT has to pause the app for maintenance or a security issue, users see one of two notices:

  • RedUnder maintenance "Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira is temporarily unavailable". Nothing saved is lost.
  • YellowChanges paused "Changes are paused for maintenance to keep your data safe." Viewing keeps working.

Follow the current status on superapps.statuspage.io.

Export data

  • Documentation: the Export tab creates HTML, PDF, CSV and JSON files of the analysed workflows (see the User guide). Exports contain names of users, groups and fields, so keep them internal.
  • App data: the app has no export or import of its own data (plans, snapshots, notes). Your workflows themselves always stay in Jira.

Uninstall the app

  1. Open Apps › Manage your apps, find Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira and click Uninstall.
  2. Workflow changes you applied stay in Jira. Roll back any plan you don't want to keep before you uninstall: the backups are deleted with the app.
  3. Atlassian deletes the app's stored data after its retention period (see Security & privacy).

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Workflow Analyzer – FAQ & troubleshooting
body:
For: everyone who uses the app. You will learn: answers to common questions and what to do when the app shows a message. Click a question to open it.

 2

Access and licence

I can't find the app in my project.

Look in Project settings › Apps › Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira. You only see project settings if you are an admin of that project. If the entry is missing for everyone, ask your Jira admin whether the app is installed on your site.

 "No access to this page"
  • "You need project administrator permissions to use the Workflow Analyzer." The app shows workflow details only to admins of the project and to Jira admins. Ask your Jira admin to give you the "Administer projects" permission in this project (usually through the project role Administrators).
  • "You need Jira administrator permissions to use the site-wide analysis." The site-wide page is for Jira admins only. Project admins use the app in Project settings › Apps of their project.
 "Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira needs an active licence"

The Marketplace subscription for this site is not active. A Jira admin can start a free trial or subscribe under Apps › Manage your apps. Your saved plans, snapshots and notes are kept.

 "Temporarily unavailable" or "Changes are paused for maintenance to keep your data safe."

SUPERPORT has paused the app for maintenance or a security issue: either completely ("temporarily unavailable") or read-only (you can still view everything, changes are paused). Nothing you saved is lost. Check the current status on superapps.statuspage.io and try again later.

Analysis

Can the analysis break anything?

No. Reading and analysing never change Jira. Only these actions write to Jira, and only after you confirm them: applying or rolling back an Autopilot plan, Create Jira tasks and the issue resolution repair.

 Where is the old XML upload?

You don't need it anymore. The app reads the workflow configuration directly from Jira, always up to date. Click Refresh in the header to read it again.

 Why does the access simulator say "depends"?

The result depends on data of the actual issue (field values, history) or on a condition of another app that is only checked when the transition runs. The reason is shown next to each transition.

 What does "not found" mean in Dependencies?

The workflow rule refers to a group, user, field or other object that no longer exists on the site (deleted or renamed). Such rules may block a transition for everyone. Update the rule. For deleted groups and inactive users, Auto-fix findings in the Autopilot can remove the reference for you.

 I don't see the Flow, Compare or Changes tab.
  • Flow and Changes are only on project pages, not on the site-wide page ("Live flow data is available on the project page.").
  • Compare appears only when at least two workflows are analysed.

Changes and the Autopilot

Why can't I apply a plan?
  • "Only a Jira admin can change this company-managed workflow. You can still plan and validate the change and hand it over." Ask a Jira admin to apply it.
  • "This workflow is shared with other projects – please confirm first." Tick I understand – apply for all these projects if the change is right for all of them.
  • "Jira would reject this plan – nothing will be changed": Jira found a problem, listed below the message. Adjust the plan (for example with exact status, transition or group names) and create it again. Operations marked ✕ are not possible and are skipped.
  • The plan is Greyexpired: plans older than 7 days can no longer be applied. Click Plan again on the current version.
 "Someone changed this workflow after the plan was applied."

You are rolling back a plan, but the workflow was changed again afterwards. A rollback restores the state before your plan and also undoes those later changes. Choose Roll back anyway only if that is what you want. Otherwise, talk to the colleague first or create a new plan.

 "There is no automatic fix for these findings."

Some findings need a decision, for example simplifying a complex transition. Follow the Recommendation of the finding, use a template in the Autopilot, or click Create Jira tasks to plan the work. With AI on, Fix with AI writes a change request for you.

 Can the Autopilot change JMWE, JSU or ScriptRunner rules?

No. The app shows and analyses rules of other apps, but the Autopilot cannot edit them. Change them in that app. The Autopilot can remove references to deleted groups and inactive users from Jira's own rules.

Issue resolutions

"The Resolution field is not on this issue's edit screen. A Jira admin can repair it."

Project admins can only change the resolution through the issue's edit screen. Either add the Resolution field to the edit screen, or ask a Jira admin to run the repair: Jira admins can repair any issue, without notification mails.

 Why can't I undo setting a resolution?

Jira Cloud cannot take a resolution back without moving the issue. That's why the app asks you to check your choices before you click Yes, repair. Clearing a resolution can be undone. If the app says "Jira cannot clear a resolution in place, and no transition into this issue's status clears it", move the issue out of its status and back.

AI and Rovo

I don't see any AI features. The tab says "Explanations".

The AI features are off by default. Only a Jira admin can switch them on: Jira settings › Apps › Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira (site-wide) › AI features. After that, reload the page. Every feature without AI works either way.

 "The monthly AI quota is used up" or "AI features are temporarily turned off by the app vendor"
  • "The monthly AI quota is used up. It is available again from the 1st of next month." Your site has used its monthly AI budget, which is included in the subscription. Jira admins see the usage on the AI features card.
  • "AI features are temporarily turned off by the app vendor. Please try again later." SUPERPORT has turned the AI off for a while. Your admin's setting is kept and applies again automatically.

Everything without AI keeps working in both cases.

 "Rovo is not enabled on this site." or the Rovo agent says a project "is not available".
  • The Rovo agent Workflow Analyst needs Rovo on your site. Without Rovo, use the assistant inside the app.
  • The agent only answers about projects you administer (or all projects, if you are a Jira admin). Give it the project key, for example "IDE".

Export and notes

"The PNG could not be created. Try SVG instead, or reload the page."

Download the diagram as SVG or Mermaid instead, or reload the page and try PNG again.

 Who sees my team notes?

All admins of the project who open the app. Notes can also be included in exports (Include › Team notes).

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Workflow Analyzer – Security & privacy
body:
For: Jira admins, security and data protection officers. You will learn: where the app runs, what it stores, which permissions it uses and why, how the AI works, and what happens when you uninstall it.

 2

In short

#E9F7EF :lock:
  • GreenRuns on Atlassian The app runs entirely on Atlassian Forge. It sends no data outside Atlassian and uses no third-party services, analytics or external servers.
  • All app data is kept in Atlassian's Forge storage of your installation.
  • The only personal data the app stores are Atlassian account IDs. Names are looked up from Jira when they are shown.
  • The AI features are off by default and run on Atlassian (Forge LLMs and Rovo).
  • The app collects no credentials, API tokens or keys.

Where the app runs and where data is stored

QuestionAnswer
Where does the app run?Entirely on Atlassian Forge ("Runs on Atlassian"). The app declares no external servers or outbound connections.
Does the app send data outside Atlassian?No. No external calls, no analytics, no third-party services. The app's pages load no files from outside Atlassian.
Where is data stored?In the Forge hosted storage of your installation. Nothing is stored outside Atlassian.
Data residencyForge hosted storage follows the data residency location of your Jira site.
Sub-processorsNone besides Atlassian.
EncryptionIn transit and at rest, provided by Atlassian Forge.

What the app stores

DataContentsPersonal data
Change plans and backupsOperations, workflow name, health score before and after, a backup of the workflow for rollback, who created, applied or rolled back the planAccount ID
Bulk changesAs above, for site-wide bulk changesAccount ID
SnapshotsWorkflow configuration at a point in time, label, who saved itAccount ID
Team notesText per transition, authorAccount ID, free text written by your team
Preferences and last visitLanguage and display preferences, last-seen markersAccount ID
AI switchOn or off, who changed it and when (last 50 changes)Account ID
Monitoring, Jira tasks created from findings, resolution repair historyProject IDs, finding keys, keys of changed issues, who did itAccount ID
AI usage meterRequests, tokens and cost per monthNo

The app does not store issue content, comments, attachments, display names or email addresses. Copies of workflow configuration (snapshots, rollback backups) can contain account IDs of users that your workflow rules refer to.

Permissions the app uses, and why

ScopeWhy
read:jira-workRead projects, workflows, statuses, transitions, rules, screens, fields, resolutions, roles and issue counts to build the analysis.
write:jira-workOnly on your explicit action: create Jira tasks from findings (Create Jira tasks) and repair the resolution of issues (Review & repair).
read:jira-userCheck the signed-in user's permissions and show the names of users and groups referenced in workflow rules (for example inactive users).
manage:jira-configurationWorkflows are site configuration in Jira. Applying and rolling back Autopilot plans needs this scope. Company-managed workflows can only be changed by Jira admins. Every change is confirmed by the user, validated by Jira and backed up.
storage:appThe app's own data in Forge storage (see the table above).
report:personal-dataAtlassian's Personal Data Reporting API: the app reports the account IDs it stores and deletes them when Atlassian reports an account as closed.

The app also declares Atlassian's Forge LLM module and the Rovo agent Workflow Analyst. Both are AI features and stay off until a Jira admin switches them on.

Who can see and change what

  • The project and the user always come from Atlassian's signed context, never from the browser.
  • Every request checks the caller's Jira permissions again: project admins for their own project, Jira admins for the site-wide page and company-managed workflows. Users without these permissions see nothing.
  • Changes happen only after explicit confirmation. Jira validates them first, a backup and a snapshot are stored, and a rollback never silently overwrites later changes by colleagues.
  • Without an active Marketplace licence the app refuses every request.

Personal data and GDPR

  • The app stores the Atlassian account IDs of users who create plans, notes or snapshots, run repairs or change the AI switch.
  • The app uses Atlassian's Personal Data Reporting API. It regularly reports the stored account IDs to Atlassian. When Atlassian reports an account as closed, the app deletes that person's preferences and visit markers and removes the account ID from every record (plans, notes, snapshots, logs). The content itself stays.
  • You are the data controller. SUPERPORT does not receive your data.
  • You can delete plans, snapshots and notes in the app.

AI features

  • Off by default. Only Jira admins can switch them on, on the site-wide page. Every change of the switch is logged with who and when.
  • Runs on Atlassian. When AI is on, the relevant workflow configuration and the user's question go to Forge LLMs (Claude, run by Atlassian) or to Rovo. Neither is a third party to you, and nothing leaves Atlassian.
  • Reviewed by people. AI answers are labelled "AI-generated – please review". The AI never changes Jira without the user's confirmation.
  • Limited. A monthly AI budget per site applies. SUPERPORT can also turn the AI off temporarily.

Retention and uninstall

  • When the app is uninstalled, Atlassian soft-deletes its Forge hosted storage and deletes it permanently after the retention period. See Atlassian's hosted storage data lifecycle.
  • Workflow changes you applied stay in your Jira.

Exports

Documentation exports (HTML, PDF, CSV, JSON) are files you download and store yourself. They contain names of users, groups and fields from your workflows, so store them in internal spaces only.

Legal and contact

  • End User License Agreement and privacy policy (covers all SUPERPORT apps)
  • Security questions and reports: support portal or support@superport.digital (subject "Security")
  • Status and incident communication: superapps.statuspage.io
  • Vendor: SUPERPORT P.C., Athens, Greece · www.superport.digital

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira · SUPERPORT

title: Workflow Analyzer – Release notes
body:
For: everyone who uses the app. You will learn: what changed in each version, newest first. Updates install automatically; you don't need to do anything unless a version says so.

 2

4.2.0 – 24 November 2026

GreenNEW NAME

The app's new name and logo.

  • The app is now called Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira. The new name appears in the Jira menus (Project settings › Apps and Jira settings › Apps), in the app and in exports. Nothing else changes.
  • This is the version prepared for the Atlassian Marketplace.

4.0.0 – 24 November 2026

Action for Jira admins: this version adds one permission, report personal data. Jira asks a Jira admin to approve it before the update is installed.

GreenNEW New

  • Exports in plain language. HTML, PDF, CSV and JSON exports now explain each workflow so that everyone understands it: a verdict, the usual path from start to done (who may take each step, what Jira checks, what happens automatically and why), other routes, prioritised improvements with the reason and the fix, every transition explained and a glossary. The full rule table follows for administrators.
  • Exports cover what you export. Score, apps and dependencies in an export refer only to the exported workflows or selection.
  • Tabs in a clearer order: understand (Overview to Explanations), check and change (Health check to Changes), document (Export, Guide).
  • Overview reworked: a new Dependencies tile (groups, roles, fields, users … with the number "not found") and the Health check card.
  • "New here?" tip on the Overview starts the tour or opens the guide.
  • Personal data: the app now stores account IDs only, never names, and reports them to Atlassian's Personal Data Reporting API. Data of closed accounts is erased automatically.

BlueIMPROVED Improved and fixed

  • PDF exports are much faster, and large exports offer a Save file button.
  • Layout fixes in the HTML export (table headers, toolbar).
  • Downloading the diagram as PNG works inside Jira, and errors are shown.
  • The Overview shows when each workflow was last changed.
  • Diagram labels no longer cover status boxes.
  • Daily monitoring no longer reports a change with 0 differences.
  • Flow counts only the issues of the workflow's own issue types.
  • The Overview no longer counts hints as warnings.
  • Compare calls workflows "identical" only when there are no differences.
  • Jira tasks from findings are created in the project you are working in.
  • With AI off, the Rovo agent tells you exactly where a Jira admin can switch it on.
  • Clickable rows can be used with the keyboard.

3.0.0 – 23 November 2026

  • GreenNEW Paid via Atlassian. The app is licensed through the Atlassian Marketplace. Without an active licence it shows a notice; your saved data is kept.
  • GreenNEW AI budget included. Each site gets a monthly AI budget (€20 by default) at no extra cost. The AI features card shows this month's budget and usage.
  • BlueIMPROVED The in-app guide explains the app status notices and what to do when a licence is needed.

2.4.0 – 16 November 2026

  • GreenNEW AI switch for Jira admins. The AI features are off by default. Jira admins switch them on or off on the site-wide page; every change is logged with who and when.
  • GreenNEW No AI buttons while AI is off. The app hides every AI entry point, and the AI assistant tab becomes Explanations. Everything without AI works as before.
  • GreenNEW A monthly AI limit per site, shown next to the switch.
  • BlueIMPROVED AI answers are labelled "AI-generated – please review".
  • BlueIMPROVED Clear notices during maintenance, with a link to the status page.

Earlier versions – October 2026

26 October 2026

  • GreenNEW Issue resolutions: find issues that are Done but Unresolved, or open but resolved, and repair them without changing their status (Health check › Issue resolutions › Review & repair), with a repair history. Clearing a resolution can be undone.
  • GreenNEW New checks: Done transitions that clear the resolution, and Done transitions that fire the Generic Event (so no "resolved" or "closed" emails are sent). Auto-fix sets the resolution and the "Issue Resolved" event.

24 October 2026: first version

  • Live workflow analysis straight from Jira: Overview, Diagram, Transitions, Dependencies, Access, Flow, Compare.
  • Health check with one-click fixes and Jira tasks from findings.
  • Autopilot: change plans with dry run, Jira validation, apply and one-click rollback.
  • Site-wide analysis and bulk changes for Jira admins.
  • Rovo agent Workflow Analyst.
  • Exports as HTML, PDF, CSV and JSON; everything in English and German.

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

Documentation by George Papasotiriou, developer of Workflow Analyzer & Autopilot for Jira · SUPERPORT
